answer: A nonrefundable activation fee prices each eligible identity. Before an agent can earn rewards for ember alerts near juniper stands or tundra fire mapping, validators check that a finalized burn of F tokens names its public key. The burn activates only that key, so N eligible identities cost N times F even if they share an operator. The fee deters farming only when it exceeds the expected extra profit per identity; rebates or free activations would undermine it.
